newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian investors clash with armed civilians.
newsitem.headline: Albanian investors clash with armed civilians.

text.p: Armed Albanian civilians attacked several thousand ruined investors who were demonstrating in a southern town on Thursday and at least six people were injured, witnesses said.

They said the civilians were armed with wooden sticks and iron bars when they swooped on a crowd of about 3,000 people protesting in Fieri, 120 km (75 miles) south of Tirana, at the loss of their savings in collapsed pyramid investement schemes.
The crowd waving white and red roses had been marching to demand that the government reimburse them. They threw stones back at their civilian attackers, who fled.
Three of the injured protesters were treated in hospital. Two were released but a 50-year-old man was kept in hospital and risked losing an eye, doctors said.
The crowd, chanting "We want our money" and "Down with the government," later marched near the police station where police were on standby but did not intervene.
Protesters blamed ruling Democratic Party supporters for the attack. "We came out with flowers and they attacked us," one demonstrators complained.
The crowd marched back to the main square, led by a protester with his face covered with blood who refused to go to hospital.
Three people were killed earlier this week and about 150 were injured when anti-government protesters clashed with riot police in the town of Vlore, further to the south.
